:::{#thm-nb-poisson-limit}
#### The negative binomial converges to the Poisson

Let the population [mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) be $\mean > 0$, and let $Y_\overdisp \sim \NegBin(\mean, \overdisp)$.
Then for each $y \in \set{0, 1, 2, \dots}$,
as $\overdisp \rightarrow \infty$,
the negative binomial PMF converges to the [Poisson](#def-poisson) PMF (@eq-pois-pmf):

$$\lim_{\overdisp \rightarrow \infty} \P(Y_\overdisp = y) = \frac{\mean^{y} e^{-\mean}}{y!}$$

:::

::: proof

Choose a value $y$ of $Y_\overdisp$.
In @def-nb, the first factor $\mean^y / y!$ does not depend on $\overdisp$.
For the second factor,
$\gammafn(\overdisp + y) = \gammafn(\overdisp) \prod_{k=0}^{y-1} (\overdisp + k)$,
by applying $\gammafn(x + 1) = x\,\gammafn(x)$ $y$ times
(for $y = 0$, the product is empty and equals 1), so:

$$
\ba
\frac{\gammafn(\overdisp + y)}{\gammafn(\overdisp) \cdot (\overdisp + \mean)^y}
&= \frac{\gammafn(\overdisp) \prod_{k=0}^{y-1} (\overdisp + k)}{\gammafn(\overdisp) \cdot (\overdisp + \mean)^y}
&& (\gammafn(x + 1) = x\,\gammafn(x) \text{, applied } y \text{ times}) \\
&= \prod_{k=0}^{y-1} \frac{\overdisp + k}{\overdisp + \mean}
&& (\text{cancel } \gammafn(\overdisp) \text{; one factor of } \overdisp + \mean \text{ per } k) \\
&= \prod_{k=0}^{y-1} \frac{1 + k/\overdisp}{1 + \mean/\overdisp}
&& (\text{divide each numerator and denominator by } \overdisp) \\
&\rightarrow \prod_{k=0}^{y-1} \frac{1 + 0}{1 + 0}
&& (k/\overdisp \rightarrow 0 \text{ and } \mean/\overdisp \rightarrow 0 \text{; finitely many factors}) \\
&= 1
&& (\text{simplify})
\ea
$$

For the third factor, write $x \eqdef \mean/\overdisp$,
so $x \rightarrow 0$ as $\overdisp \rightarrow \infty$, and $\overdisp = \mean/x$:

$$
\ba
\log\paren{\paren{1 + \frac{\mean}{\overdisp}}^{-\overdisp}}
&= -\overdisp \log\paren{1 + \frac{\mean}{\overdisp}}
&& (\text{log of a power}) \\
&= -\mean \cdot \frac{\log(1 + x)}{x}
&& (\text{substitute } \overdisp = \mean/x) \\
&\rightarrow -\mean \cdot 1
&& (\textstyle\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \log(1 + x)/x = 1 \text{, the derivative of } \log(1 + x) \text{ at } x = 0) \\
&= -\mean
&& (\text{simplify})
\ea
$$

so, since the exponential function is continuous,
$\paren{1 + \mean/\overdisp}^{-\overdisp} \rightarrow \expf{-\mean}$.
Each of the three factors has a limit, so their product does too:

$$
\ba
\lim_{\overdisp \rightarrow \infty} \P(Y_\overdisp = y)
&= \frac{\mean^y}{y!} \cdot 1 \cdot \expf{-\mean}
&& (\text{limit of a product of convergent factors}) \\
&= \frac{\mean^{y} e^{-\mean}}{y!}
&& (\text{rearrange})
\ea
$$

which is the $\Pois(\mean)$ PMF.

:::
